answer: An agent marketplace weights votes by tokens locked in escrow, rather than by account count: splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still yields only 100 tokens of voting power. Like planting extra labels in a willow orchard, multiplying names creates no new roots. Hollow identities add no influence unless funded, so an attacker seeking one-third of voting power must acquire and lock one-third of the staked tokens, tying up capital for the lock period.
